items: Universities look at academic grades, subject requirements and whether qualifications are equivalent. \\Mathematics\\ is particularly important for engineering and \\Physics\\ may be needed for undergraduate admission.

Before you apply, make sure you check the most recent admissions guidance on the official university website.

faqs.q: \\Q1. Is there Electronics and Communication Engineering as such ECE in Ireland?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Similar programs are often offered as \\ Electronic and Computer Engineering \\ or \\ Electrical and Electronic Engineering \ \ .

faqs.q: \\Q2. How long does it take to study an ECE related degree in Ireland?\\
faqs.a: Many undergraduate honors engineering degrees are \\four years\\ long. Some integrated \\ Master of Engineering \\ routes are five years, depending on university and course structure .

faqs.q: \\Q3. What are the tuition fees for foreign students?\\
faqs.a: Others published for \\2026/27\\ include €17,900 per year at DCU for Electronic and Computer Engineering in Years 1-4 and €27,640 per year at the University of Galway including its listed levy. Additional living expenses and fees are subject to change.

faqs.q: \\Q4. What are the important subjects for admission?\\
faqs.a: \\ Mathematics is especially important. \\Physics and other sciences\\ may be required for undergraduate admission. Masters applicants typically require a related bachelor's degree and adequate technical preparation.

faqs.q: \\Q5. What kind of jobs can I find after pursuing ECE in Ireland?
faqs.a: Graduates can find jobs in \\electronics design, telecommunications, embedded systems, firmware, signal processing, semiconductor testing and network engineering. Career outcomes are based on skills, experience, vacancies and employment eligibility.
